sizeChart.measureInstructions: Place your foot on a piece of paper, trace the outline and measure the longest point (from heel to longest toe).
sizeChart.helpDescription: Size depends on the model, sock type, and personal preference. Contact us and we'll help you choose the right size.
sizeGuide.title: Size guide
sizeGuide.lead: Barefoot shoes are measured differently. Toes need room, so width is just as important as length. This guide will help you find the perfect pair.
sizeGuide.step1.title: Start with your usual size
sizeGuide.step1.body: The best sizing guide is to start with your normal shoe size. On each product page you'll find specific fit information.
sizeGuide.step1.imgAlt: Place your foot on paper and trace the outline
sizeGuide.step2.title: Trace your foot
sizeGuide.step2.body: Stand near a wall and place a piece of paper on the floor. Place your foot on the paper with heel against the wall. Trace the outline with a pencil.
sizeGuide.step2.imgAlt: Foot with heel against the wall while tracing
sizeGuide.step3.title: Keep the pencil vertical
sizeGuide.step3.body: When tracing, the pencil must be at 90° — straight up, not angled. Both feet are rarely the same — measure both and take the larger measurement.
sizeGuide.step3.imgAlt: Hold the pencil vertical while tracing for accuracy
sizeGuide.step4.title: Measure and add room
sizeGuide.step4.body: Measure the length in millimetres. Add 5–10 mm extra. If you wear thick socks, factor those in.
sizeGuide.step4.imgAlt: Measure the length and add 5–10 mm of extra room
sizeGuide.tip.title: Tip
sizeGuide.tip.body: Measure your feet in the evening — they expand throughout the day. Wear the socks you'd normally use when measuring.
sizeGuide.brands.title: Charts for each brand
sizeGuide.brands.lead: Each brand has its own sizing. On the brand page you'll find the exact chart with insole or foot length for each size.
sizeGuide.help.title: Still not sure?
sizeGuide.help.body: Write to us — we'll help personally. We have every model in our hands and know how sizes run.

newToBarefoot.title: New to barefoot?
newToBarefoot.lead: If you've never worn barefoot shoes, this page is for you.
newToBarefoot.what.title: Three things that make them different
newToBarefoot.what.lead: A conventional shoe shapes the foot. A barefoot shoe frees it.
newToBarefoot.feature1.title: Wide toe box
newToBarefoot.feature1.body: Toes need room to splay. The wide toe box restores the natural shape of the foot.
newToBarefoot.feature2.title: Zero drop
newToBarefoot.feature2.body: In barefoot shoes heel and toes are at the same level, just like walking barefoot on a flat surface.
newToBarefoot.feature3.title: Thin, flexible sole
newToBarefoot.feature3.body: The thin sole lets you feel the ground. The foot responds naturally.
newToBarefoot.transition.title: How to transition safely
newToBarefoot.transition.lead: You can't just put them on and carry on with your usual schedule. Feet need time to strengthen.
newToBarefoot.transition.week1.title: Weeks 1–2: Start slowly
newToBarefoot.transition.week1.body: Wear them 1–2 hours a day for everyday activities. Don't run. Fatigue is a sign you're doing more than you should.
newToBarefoot.transition.week3.title: Weeks 3–4: Build gradually
newToBarefoot.transition.week3.body: If you feel good, increase to 3–4 hours. Include short walks.
newToBarefoot.transition.month2.title: Month 2+: The foot starts to change
newToBarefoot.transition.month2.body: You gradually replace conventional shoes. Feet grow stronger, gait becomes more stable.
newToBarefoot.mistakes.title: Common mistakes
newToBarefoot.mistake1.title: Over-wearing at the start
newToBarefoot.mistake1.body: Pain after the first week almost always means: too much, too fast.
newToBarefoot.mistake2.title: Running before walking
newToBarefoot.mistake2.body: Barefoot running is an advanced step. First strengthen feet with walking.
newToBarefoot.mistake3.title: Expecting quick results
newToBarefoot.mistake3.body: Transition takes months. The body doesn't adapt overnight.
newToBarefoot.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
newToBarefoot.faq.1.q: Are barefoot shoes suitable for everyone?
newToBarefoot.faq.1.a: For almost everyone — but the transition must be gradual.
newToBarefoot.faq.2.a: Mild muscle soreness at the start is normal. Sharp pain means you should stop.
newToBarefoot.faq.3.a: After 2–3 months of regular walking wear. Start with short intervals.
newToBarefoot.faq.4.q: Can I wear them to work?
newToBarefoot.faq.4.a: Yes — but apply the same rules. Start with a few hours and increase gradually.
newToBarefoot.cta.title: Ready to start?
newToBarefoot.cta.body: Every shoe in our store shows sole thickness, drop, and toe box width.
